subtitle: UPDATE Jul 29, 18:47 BRT, with 67 days to the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). THE DAY IS THE EXACT INVERSE OF THE ONE BEFORE: yesterday there was no national polling and the favourite's price rose 1.00pp; today the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out and the favourite's price FELL 1.00pp, to 62.50%, with the gap over Flávio easing from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. THE POLLING: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg (n=5,021, field Jul 22 to 27, 1pp margin, BR-08602/2026, cost of R$ 80,000, self-funded) has Lula 44.9% x Flávio 35.8% in the first round, a gap of 9.1pp, with Renan Santos 7.8%, Caiado 3.1% and Zema 2.8%. Lula wins the SIX [runoffs](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) he appears in, and the tightest margin is 5.3pp against JAIR Bolsonaro (49.2% to 43.9%), not against Flávio, who sits at 6.3pp. In the two scenarios without Lula, Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico), and Alckmin 45.8% x Flávio 42.7%. Approval of Lula 47.6% against 51.2% disapproval. Rejection: Flávio 52.9%, Lula 49.4% and Jair 42.6%. Against the institute's own Jul 1 round, BOTH front-runners fall and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp, all inside the 1pp margin, so the honest reading of the polling is stability. THE DIRECTION MATCHES, THE SIZE DOES NOT: the poll narrowed the gap by 0.6pp and the market narrowed by 1.10pp in the same session, and the panel records the coincidence without claiming cause. THE METHOD FINDING is in Renan Santos: 7.8% in the polling against 8.60% in price leaves the distance at 0.80pp, and in this round it narrowed on the POLLING side, which rose, and not on the price side, as had been happening. CAIADO INVERTED yesterday's signal: he rose 0.45pp in the winner book, to 2.35%, and fell 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%, on the same day the polling cut him in half, from 6% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) to 3.1%. THE INSTITUTIONAL AXIS was born inside the [PL](/en/glossary#pl)'s own convention: after Moraes gave 48 hours on Jul 28, Jair Bolsonaro's defence answered on Wednesday that he did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video, while Flávio told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters. Even so, the market on impeachment of an [STF](/en/glossary#stf) justice rose only 0.05pp, to 2.85%, in a book of USD 83,000. Total accumulated volume in the presidential book at USD 116.49M. Cross-reading with live [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) Jul 29, 21:47 UTC: the double-reading guard REJECTED the first round over a 1.00pp divergence in Renan Santos's third place and APPROVED the second with no divergence at all, so every price enters firm and there is no range in this update.

candidates.name: Lula
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 62.50% (down 1.00pp, vol USD 7.73M accumulated), with 67 days to the election. It fell on the day the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out, the exact inverse of yesterday. The gap over Flávio eased to +38.55pp. In the polling, [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg of Jul 29 (n=5,021, 1pp margin, BR-08602/2026) has him at 44.9% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and winning the six [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) scenarios he appears in, with approval of 47.6% against 51.2% disapproval.
fortes: The fresh polling has the largest sample in the window and keeps him comfortably ahead: 44.9% in the first round against 35.8% for Flávio, a gap of 9.1pp, with a 1pp margin.
He wins the SIX runoff scenarios he appears in at AtlasIntel, and none of those margins fits inside the 1pp margin of error.
Approval of his performance RISES 1.7pp against the same institute's Jul 1 round, from 45.9% to 47.6%, a move that sits outside the margin.
He dominates the Northeast in the state polls released today: 52% in Bahia and 54% in Ceará, against 18% and 23% for Flávio (Genial/Quaest and Ipsos-Ipec).
His rejection, 49.4%, sits 4.5pp above his own voting intention, while for Flávio that distance is 17.1pp.
fracos: The price FELL 1.00pp on the day the largest poll in the window came out, and the market's direction followed the poll's, which also narrowed the gap.
Against AtlasIntel's own Jul 1 round he retreats from 46.3% to 44.9%, and disapproval remains ahead of approval by the same method, 51.2% to 47.6%.
He loses São Paulo, the country's largest electoral college, in both rounds: 30% to 34% in the first and 35% to 40% in the runoff (Genial/Quaest, n=1,650, field Jul 23 to 27).
The 44.9% in the first round remains below 50% plus one vote, which means the largest-sample poll in the window still describes a runoff and not an outright win.
The São Paulo electoral court fined him R$ 15,000 for early campaigning and ordered the video taken down (Estadão, G1, Valor Econômico, Jul 29).
candidates.analise: His day mirrors the one before, and the comparison between the two sessions is the panel's finding. Yesterday no national poll came out and the price rose 1.00pp. Today the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out and the price fell 1.00pp, from 63.50% to 62.50% (vol USD 7.73M), with the gap over Flávio easing from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. Before any reading, the level caveat: 62.50% is the same level as Jul 25 and Jul 27 and sits 1.00pp below the top of the AFOS series, which marked 63.50% on Jul 26 and Jul 28. This is not a drop in level, it is the return of the point he took yesterday. By the daily close of the series, today's gap is the narrowest since Jul 24. The polling: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg (field Jul 22 to 27, n=5,021, 1pp margin, BR-08602/2026) has him at 44.9% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) against 35.8% for Flávio, a gap of 9.1pp, and has him winning the six [runoffs](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) he appears in. Here comes a data point internal to the survey that the panel is obliged to show: his tightest win is not against Flávio, it is against JAIR Bolsonaro, 49.2% to 43.9%, a margin of 5.3pp against the 6.3pp of the scenario with the son. The difference between the two scenarios, 1.0pp, sits at the edge of the margin, so this is not a tie undone but a suggestion that the father's name tests equal or better. Against the same institute's Jul 1 round, he retreats from 46.3% to 44.9% and Flávio retreats from 36.6% to 35.8%: BOTH front-runners fall, and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp. With a 1pp margin, each of those moves fits in the noise, and the honest reading of the polling is stability. What moves outside the margin is the rating: approval rises 1.7pp, from 45.9% to 47.6%, and disapproval falls 1.1pp, from 52.3% to 51.2%, with disapproval remaining ahead. On the coincidence between the fall in price and the narrowing in the poll, the panel records the direction and does NOT claim cause: the poll narrowed 0.6pp and the market narrowed 1.10pp, different sizes, and the same session carried the fallout of the artificial-intelligence video at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) and the Brazilian government's reading that the extension of the US emergency may be preparing new sanctions. Among the state polls of the day, which do not enter the national window, the picture of a split country gained the largest electoral college: he loses São Paulo in both rounds, 30% to 34% in the first and 35% to 40% in the runoff, and wins the Northeast comfortably, 52% in Bahia and 54% in Ceará. His accumulated volume at USD 7.73M, in a presidential book that adds up to USD 116.49M.

candidates.name: Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 23.95% (up 0.10pp, vol USD 7.70M accumulated), a fourth consecutive daily close on the rise in the AFOS series, up from 22.90% on Jul 25. Because the favourite fell 1.00pp, the gap against him narrowed 1.10pp and went to +38.55pp. In the polling, [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 has him at 35.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and 42.9% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), with rejection of 52.9%. He leads São Paulo in both rounds and trails badly in the Northeast.
fortes: A fourth consecutive daily close on the rise in the AFOS series, moving from 22.90% on Jul 25 to 24.00% at today's close.
The gap against him narrowed 1.10pp in the day, from +39.65pp to +38.55pp, and by the daily close of the series it is the narrowest since Jul 24.
He leads São Paulo, the country's largest electoral college, in BOTH rounds: 34% to 30% in the first and 40% to 35% in the runoff (Genial/Quaest, n=1,650, field Jul 23 to 27, BR-09998/2026).
He stayed flat at 78.00% in the first-round second-place book for a second session, which means his runoff position remains settled and not in dispute.
He received explicit backing from the PL to try to unify the Minas Gerais platform around Marcelo Aro, after the Republicanos announced Cleitinho was out of the race.
fracos: The rejection measured by AtlasIntel, 52.9%, is the highest among those tested and sits 17.1pp above his own first-round voting intention, 35.8%.
In the same survey, JAIR Bolsonaro tests better than him in the runoff, losing by 5.3pp against his own 6.3pp, even if the 1.0pp difference sits at the edge of the margin.
Against AtlasIntel's own Jul 1 round he FALLS from 36.6% to 35.8%, with no advance in the largest sample of the window.

Jair Bolsonaro's defence told the STF that he did NOT authorise the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video shown at the PL convention, which puts his campaign piece in contradiction with his own father.
He still has no running mate, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away, and vetoed his mother as a Senate alternate in the Rio arrangement to avoid association with an ally (O Globo, Jul 29).
candidates.analise: His day has two layers moving in opposite directions, and the panel needs to keep them apart. On price, it was another day of small, persistent gains: he rose 0.10pp, to 23.95% (vol USD 7.70M), and the daily close of the AFOS series records a fourth consecutive advance, moving from 22.90% on Jul 25 to 24.00% today. Because the favourite fell 1.00pp, the gap against him narrowed 1.10pp and went to +38.55pp, the narrowest since Jul 24 by the daily close. In the sub-markets the picture is one of a settled position: he stayed FLAT at 78.00% in first-round second place for a second session and FELL 1.50pp in third place, to 6.25%. A name motionless in the second-place contract and falling in the third-place one is a name the market has already decided where to put. In the polling, the layer is different. [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29 has him at 35.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), a 0.8pp retreat against the institute's Jul 1 round, and at 42.9% in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) against 49.2% for Lula. The number that weighs most is none of those: it is the 52.9% rejection, the highest among those tested, which sits 17.1pp above his own voting intention. For Lula, the same distance is 4.5pp. That describes a candidacy with a ceiling, not with a trajectory, and it is a structural constraint, not a fact of the day. There is also the finding internal to the survey: JAIR Bolsonaro loses the runoff by 5.3pp and he loses by 6.3pp, with the 1.0pp difference at the edge of the margin. By the same institute and in the same field period, the father's name does not test worse than the son's. Among the state polls, the day was good where the votes are: he leads São Paulo in both rounds, 34% to 30% in the first and 40% to 35% in the runoff. And it was bad in the Northeast, with 18% in Bahia and 23% in Ceará. On the institutional front, Wednesday collected the bill for his own convention: after Moraes gave 48 hours on Jul 28, Jair Bolsonaro's defence answered on Wednesday that he did NOT authorise the use of his image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão, Jul 29), while his campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters (Folha de S.Paulo). The panel records both positions and projects no outcome.

candidates.name: Renan Santos
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) 8.60% in the winner book (down 0.15pp, vol USD 8.59M accumulated). The number of the day is not the price, it is the DISTANCE: with 7.8% in [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, the divergence between implied probability and declared voting intention fell to 0.80pp, and in this round it narrowed on the POLLING side, which rose, not on the price side. In the sub-markets, he fell 0.40pp in second place, to 11.75%, and recovered 1.00pp in third place, to 61.50%.
fortes: The fresh polling is his second-best national reading in the window, 7.8%, behind only the 9% from Real Time on Jul 21, and it comes with the largest sample and the smallest margin in the window.
The distance between his price and the polling fell to 0.80pp, and it narrowed on the poll side, which rose, and not on the price side, as had been happening since June.
He recovered 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 61.50%, reversing part of the transfer to Caiado from the two previous sessions.
He keeps the third-highest price in the presidential book and the largest accumulated volume among the competitive names, USD 8.59M, above Lula's and Flávio's.
fracos: He fell 0.15pp in the winner contract and 0.40pp in first-round second place, which means the day's recovery was confined to the third-place book.
In the runoff, he is Lula's most comfortable scenario in the whole AtlasIntel survey: 47.6% to 30.2%, a distance of 17.4pp.
Today's 8.60% remains far below the 17.90% peak of Jun 9, so the current level is a continuation of retreat and not a fresh plateau.

The dispersion between institutes did not resolve with the largest sample in the window: 9% at Real Time, 7.8% at AtlasIntel, 6% at PoderData/Aya, 5% at BTG/Nexus and 3% at Datafolha, Gerp and Indexa all still stand.
His was the only book the capture guard rejected in the first round, with a 1.00pp divergence in third place, which points to a thin book and a wide spread in that contract.
candidates.analise: His day is the most interesting in the panel in terms of method, and the number that matters is not the price. On price, he fell 0.15pp to 8.60% (vol USD 8.59M), with a 0.40pp fall in first-round second place, to 11.75%, and a 1.00pp recovery in third place, to 61.50%. In other words, of the three books he appears in, two gave way and one returned part of what it had lost to Caiado. What actually changes is the distance this panel has tracked since June. [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, with n=5,021 and a 1pp margin, has him at 7.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno). Against 8.60% in price, the distance between implied probability and declared voting intention sits at 0.80pp. And the point worth recording is the MECHANICS, not the size: in previous weeks that distance narrowed because the price gave way, while the polling stayed at 3%; in this round it narrowed because the POLLING rose, and rose in the largest-sample poll of the window. Those are two different things happening to the same number, and the second is more relevant than the first, because it means the declared vote moved in the direction the price was already pointing. The usual caveat still holds: probability of victory and voting intention are different quantities and cannot be subtracted from one another as if they measured the same thing, and the panel records the proximity as a distance between quantities, not as anyone being right. The dispersion between institutes, on the other hand, did not resolve: 9% at Real Time on Jul 21, 7.8% at AtlasIntel today, 6% at PoderData/Aya on Jul 16, 5% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27 and 3% at [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Gerp and Indexa all still stand. Six percentage points of spread between institutes for the same name in the same month is the data point this panel cannot reduce. In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), AtlasIntel gives Lula's most comfortable scenario in the whole survey against him: 47.6% to 30.2%, 17.4pp of distance. Series caveat: 8.60% is neither a maximum nor a minimum, with a peak of 17.90% on Jun 9 and a floor of 5.30% on Apr 26. And a capture note that concerns him in particular: his third place was the ONLY book the guard rejected in the first round, with a 1.00pp divergence between the two readings, and the 61.50% published is the value that repeated in the three following readings.

candidates.name: Caiado / Haddad / Zema
candidates.header: [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket): Caiado 2.35% (up 0.45pp, vol USD 5.20M), Jair 1.05% (flat, vol USD 5.26M), Zema 0.75% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 4.57M), Michelle 0.45% (flat, vol USD 9.34M), Alckmin 0.35% (up 0.10pp, vol USD 4.94M), Camilo Santana 0.35% (down 0.05pp), Haddad 0.25% (flat, vol USD 6.38M), Tereza Cristina 0.20% (up 0.05pp), Tarcísio 0.15% (flat, vol USD 13.66M). In first-round third place, Caiado FELL 1.00pp, to 25.50%. In [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, Caiado has 3.1% and Zema 2.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno).
candidates.subtitle: Jul 29, with 67 days to go: the pack inverted the signal of the two previous days. Caiado, who had been rising in the third-place book and falling in the winner book, did the opposite today: he RISES 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35%, and FALLS 1.00pp in third place, to 25.50%. And the polling of the day went against him: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) has him at 3.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), half the 6% from [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) two days earlier, and in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) it has him losing 48.2% to 38.9%, far from the [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) of 45% to 43% in that survey. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 gained a third measurement and landed on [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha)'s side. Politically, though, it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas cleared allies to back his candidacy (CNN Brasil) and he began attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure (Folha de S.Paulo). Zema rose 0.20pp, to 0.75%, and today's national poll puts yesterday's state number in perspective: in the national runoff he loses to Lula 48.6% to 39.6%. Haddad stayed flat at 0.25% in the winner book and ROSE 0.35pp in first-round second place, to 1.20%, on the same day AtlasIntel showed him in a statistical tie with Flávio in a scenario without Lula, 44.3% to 43.7%.

caiado.label: CAIADO ([PSD](/en/glossary#psd)), presidential Poly 2.35% (up 0.45pp, vol USD 5.20M) | first-round third place 25.50% (down 1.00pp) | candidate confirmed on Jul 26, with Kassab as running mate | latest national poll: AtlasIntel Jul 29, first round 3.1% and runoff Lula 48.2% x Caiado 38.9%
caiado.fortes: The signal flipped in favour of the contract that matters most: he RISES 0.45pp in the winner book, to 2.35%, after two sessions of rising only in the placement book. The 2.35% of this capture sits above every daily close of the AFOS series since Jun 20, when the series marked 2.30%, and the series maximum is 2.40%, from Apr 14 and Jun 19. In other words, his price returned to the high end of its own historical band. Politically it was the pack's best day: Tarcísio de Freitas cleared allies to back his candidacy (CNN Brasil, Jul 29), and he adopted the strategy of attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure (Folha de S.Paulo), including saying that Flávio lost his own convention to an Argentine and an avatar.
caiado.fracos: The polling of the day cut him in half and undid the most favourable scenario he had. [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, with n=5,021 and a 1pp margin, has him at 3.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), against 6% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) two days earlier, and in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) it has him losing 48.2% to 38.9%, a distance of 9.3pp, far from the [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) of 45% to 43% in that survey and closer to the 47% to 40% of [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) on Jul 24. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus and Datafolha gained the third measurement it was missing and landed on Datafolha's side. And the price in the third-place book GAVE WAY 1.00pp, to 25.50%, returning part of the gain of the two previous days. Scale caveat: 2.35% remains a low level in absolute terms, in a book where the favourite is worth 62.50%.

haddad.label: HADDAD ([PT](/en/glossary#pt)), presidential Poly 0.25% (flat, vol USD 6.38M) | first-round second place 1.20% (up 0.35pp) | not tested in the main first-round scenario by any national poll | AtlasIntel Jul 29, scenario WITHOUT Lula: Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a statistical tie
haddad.fortes: He had the pack's best polling number, and it is NATIONAL, unlike Zema's yesterday. In one of the two [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) scenarios without Lula in [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, he appears at 44.3% against 43.7% for Flávio, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) inside the 1pp margin, and it is the tightest result of the whole round. His price in the first-round second-place book ROSE 0.35pp, to 1.20%, on the same day.
haddad.fracos: The winner contract did not move: it stayed at 0.25% for a second session. Rising on the chance of reaching the runoff and not rising on the chance of winning is a crossed signal, and in his case there is an aggravating factor for the reading: he is not a presidential candidate, he is running for governor of São Paulo, and in that race Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) of Jul 29 has him at 26% against 41% for Tarcísio in the first round. The scenario without Lula is a polling hypothesis, not a candidacy under way, and the panel records the number without treating it as a real race.

zema.label: ZEMA ([Novo](/en/glossary#novo)), presidential Poly 0.75% (up 0.20pp, vol USD 4.57M) | first-round third place 4.50% (down 0.10pp) | AtlasIntel Jul 29: first round 2.8% and runoff Lula 48.6% x Zema 39.6% | candidate confirmed by Novo on Jul 27, still with NO running mate, deadline Aug 5
zema.fortes: He rose 0.20pp in the presidential contract, to 0.75%, and holds the second-highest price in the pack, behind only Caiado among those actually running for president. He intends to step up his presence in the Minas Gerais governor's campaign (Folha de S.Paulo, Jul 29), a state where Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) showed him the day before numerically ahead of Lula in a state-level runoff scenario.
zema.fracos: Today's national poll puts yesterday's state number in perspective, and the perspective is harsh: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) has him at 2.8% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and has him losing the national [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) to Lula 48.6% to 39.6%, a distance of 9.0pp. A runoff in Minas and a national runoff are different questions, and today's is the second. Series caveat, and it is a big one: his maximum in the AFOS series is 10.10%, from Apr 26, so 0.75% is at less than a tenth of that level and the 0.20pp gain is little money in absolute terms. He still has NO running mate announced, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away.

candidates.analise: The pack inverted the signal of the two previous sessions, and the inversion matters more than the size of the numbers. Caiado had been rising sharply in the third-place book and falling in the winner book; today he did exactly the opposite, RISING 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35%, and FALLING 1.00pp in third place, to 25.50%. On the other side of that ledger is Renan Santos, who recovered 1.00pp in that same book. The detail that gives the move meaning is the polling, and it went against Caiado: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel) of Jul 29, with n=5,021 and a 1pp margin, has him at 3.1% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno), half the 6% from [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) two days earlier, and in the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) it has him losing 48.2% to 38.9%. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus (45% to 43%) and [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha) (47% to 40%) gained the third measurement it was missing, and it landed on Datafolha's side. In other words, the winner price rose on the day the polling got worse, and the panel records the divergence of direction without picking which of the two is right. Politically it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas cleared allies to back his candidacy and he began attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure. The pack's best polling number, though, belongs neither to him nor to Zema, but to Haddad, for a reason of method: it is NATIONAL. In one of AtlasIntel's two scenarios without Lula, Haddad ties statistically with Flávio, 44.3% to 43.7%, the tightest result of the whole round, and his price in the first-round second-place book rose 0.35pp, to 1.20%, while the winner contract stayed flat at 0.25%. The caveat is that this scenario is a polling hypothesis and not a candidacy under way. Zema rose 0.20pp, to 0.75%, and today's national poll reframes yesterday's state number: in the national runoff he loses 48.6% to 39.6%. Michelle stayed at 0.45%, Jair at 1.05%, Alckmin rose 0.10pp to 0.35% and Camilo Santana fell 0.05pp to 0.35%. The usual method caveat: these are prices between 0.15% and 2.35% in a book where the favourite is worth 62.50%, so a change in percentage points looks large in relative terms and is small in money.
fortes: Caiado inverted the signal and rose 0.45pp in the contract that matters most, the winner book, going to 2.35%, above every daily close of the AFOS series since Jun 20.
Haddad had the pack's best polling number and it is NATIONAL: a statistical tie with Flávio, 44.3% to 43.7%, in a runoff scenario without Lula in AtlasIntel of Jul 29.
Tarcísio de Freitas cleared allies to back Caiado's presidential candidacy (CNN Brasil, Jul 29).
Zema rose 0.20pp, to 0.75%, and Alckmin rose 0.10pp, to 0.35%, in the same session in which the favourite gave way 1.00pp.
fracos: The largest-sample poll in the window cut Caiado in half: 3.1% in the first round against 6% at BTG/Nexus two days earlier, and a runoff of 48.2% to 38.9%.
The divergence over Caiado gained a third measurement and it landed on Datafolha's side, which undoes the national statistical tie the panel had recorded since Jul 27.
No name in the pack goes above 2.35% in the presidential contract, against 62.50% for the favourite, and none appears ahead of Lula in any national runoff in AtlasIntel.
Zema loses the national runoff 48.6% to 39.6% and still has no running mate, with the Aug 5 deadline less than a week away; his maximum in the AFOS series is 10.10%, from Apr 26.
Haddad rose in the second-place book and stayed flat in the winner book, and the scenario that favours him is a polling hypothesis, not a candidacy under way.

quadroComparativo.p: FRESH POLLING and it is the largest sample in the window: [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg of Jul 29 (n=5,021, field Jul 22-27, 1pp margin, BR-08602/2026) has 44.9% in the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno) and victory in the SIX [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno) scenarios he appears in, the tightest being 5.3pp against JAIR Bolsonaro (49.2% to 43.9%) and not the 6.3pp against Flávio. Approval 47.6% x disapproval 51.2%. Against the institute's Jul 1 round, he retreats from 46.3% to 44.9%, inside the margin. Among the state polls of Wednesday: he loses São Paulo 30% x 34% in the first round and 35% x 40% in the runoff (Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest), n=1,650, BR-09998/2026); he wins Bahia 52% x 18% and Ceará 54% x 23% (Ipsos-Ipec, n=800, BR-07235/2026).

The gap over Flávio eased from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. This is not a drop in level: 62.50% is the same level as Jul 25 and Jul 27 and the top of the AFOS series marked 63.50% on Jul 26 and Jul 28. quadroComparativo.s: 67 days to the election. The direction of the price matches the direction of the polling, which also narrowed the gap, but the sizes differ: 0.6pp in the poll against 1.10pp in the market. The panel records the coincidence and claims no cause, because the same session carried the artificial-intelligence video case at the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) and the government's reading that the extension of the US emergency may be preparing new sanctions. Live [Polymarket](/en/glossary#polymarket) Jul 29, 21:47 UTC.

quadroComparativo.s: Decisive method caveat: with USD 83,000 in accumulated volume against USD 116.49M in the presidential book, neither the rise nor the stillness sustains a narrative. cruzamento: Jul 29 was the exact inverse of the day before, and the inversion is the finding itself. Yesterday there was NO national polling and the favourite's price ROSE 1.00pp. On Wednesday the national poll with the largest sample in the window came out and the favourite's price FELL 1.00pp, from 63.50% to 62.50% (vol USD 7.73M), with the gap over Flávio easing from +39.65pp to +38.55pp. Before any reading, the level caveat, because it avoids a mistake this panel has already made: 62.50% is not a drop in level, it is the same level as Jul 25 and Jul 27, and the top of the AFOS series marked 63.50% on Jul 26 and Jul 28. By the daily close of the series, today's gap is the narrowest since Jul 24. THE POLLING OF THE DAY is [AtlasIntel](/en/glossary#atlasintel)/Bloomberg (field Jul 22 to 27, n=5,021, 1pp margin, 95% confidence, BR-08602/2026, cost of R$ 80,000, self-funded), and it is the largest sample in the window, ahead of the 5,000 of the institute's own Jul 1 round, with the smallest margin, tied at 1pp with that same round. In the [first round](/en/glossary#primeiro-turno): Lula 44.9%, Flávio Bolsonaro 35.8%, Renan Santos 7.8%, Ronaldo Caiado 3.1%, Romeu Zema 2.8%, Samara Martins 2.1% and Augusto Cury 1.6%. In a scenario reduced to five names, Lula goes to 47.4% and Flávio to 37.0%. In the [runoff](/en/glossary#segundo-turno), Lula wins the SIX scenarios he appears in, and here is the data point the panel is obliged to highlight: his tightest margin is NOT against Flávio, it is against JAIR Bolsonaro, 49.2% to 43.9%, a difference of 5.3pp against the 6.3pp of the scenario with the son. The distance between the two scenarios, 1.0pp, sits at the edge of the margin, so this undoes no tie and instead suggests that, by the same institute and in the same field period, the father's name tests equal to or better than the son's. In the two scenarios WITHOUT Lula, Haddad 44.3% x Flávio 43.7%, a [statistical tie](/en/glossary#empate-tecnico) inside the margin, and Alckmin 45.8% x Flávio 42.7%. Rejection is the round's hardest number: Flávio 52.9%, Lula 49.4% and Jair 42.6%. And the comparison that matters more than the contest between institutes: Flávio's rejection sits 17.1pp above his own first-round voting intention, 35.8%, while for Lula that distance is 4.5pp, 49.4% against 44.9%. That is a structural constraint, not a data point of the day. Against the same institute's Jul 1 round, BOTH front-runners fall, Lula from 46.3% to 44.9% and Flávio from 36.6% to 35.8%, and the first-round gap narrows from 9.7pp to 9.1pp. In the direct runoff, the gap moves from 6.5pp to 6.3pp. With a 1pp margin, each of those moves fits in the noise, and the honest reading of the polling is STABILITY, not advance or retreat. What moves outside the margin is the government rating: Lula's approval rises 1.7pp, from 45.9% to 47.6%, and disapproval falls 1.1pp, from 52.3% to 51.2%, keeping disapproval ahead by the same method. ON THE COINCIDENCE between the fall in price and the narrowing in the poll, the panel records the direction and does NOT claim cause, for two reasons. First, the sizes differ: the poll narrowed the gap by 0.6pp and the market narrowed by 1.10pp. Second, the same session carried two other events capable of moving price, and the panel has no instrument to separate the contributions. Picking a cause here would be inventing precision the data does not have. THE METHOD FINDING OF THE DAY is in Renan Santos, and it is about the mechanics of convergence, not the level. With 7.8% in the polling and 8.60% in price, the distance between implied probability and declared voting intention fell to 0.80pp. In previous weeks that distance narrowed because the PRICE gave way, while the polling stayed at 3%; in this round it narrowed because the POLLING rose, and rose in the largest-sample poll of the window. Those are two different things happening to the same number, and the second is more relevant, because it means the declared vote moved in the direction the price was already pointing. It still holds that probability of victory and voting intention are different quantities, that they do not subtract from one another as if they measured the same thing, and that convergence is proof of no one being right. The dispersion between institutes, incidentally, did not resolve with the largest sample in the window: 9% at Real Time on Jul 21, 7.8% at AtlasIntel today, 6% at PoderData/Aya on Jul 16, 5% at [BTG/Nexus](/en/glossary#nexus-btg) on Jul 27 and 3% at [Datafolha](/en/glossary#datafolha), Gerp and Indexa all still stand. Six percentage points of spread between institutes for the same name in the same month is the data point this panel cannot reduce, and it is more informative than any average. THE THIRD AXIS is Caiado, and he inverted the signal of the two previous sessions. He had been rising sharply in the third-place book and falling in the winner book; today he RISES 0.45pp in the winner, to 2.35%, and FALLS 1.00pp in first-round third place, to 25.50%, with Renan Santos recovering 1.00pp in that same book. The 2.35% of this capture sits above every daily close of the AFOS series since Jun 20, when the series marked 2.30%, and the series maximum is 2.40%. Except that the polling of the day went against him, and hard: 3.1% in the first round, half the 6% BTG/Nexus measured two days earlier, and a runoff of 48.2% to 38.9%, a distance of 9.3pp, far from the statistical tie of 45% to 43% in that survey and closer to the 47% to 40% of Datafolha on Jul 24. The divergence the panel recorded on Jul 27 between Nexus and Datafolha gained the third measurement it was missing and it landed on Datafolha's side. Price rising and polling worsening on the same day is a divergence of direction, and the panel records both without choosing which is right. Politically, though, it was his best day: Tarcísio de Freitas cleared allies to back his presidential candidacy (CNN Brasil) and he adopted the strategy of attacking Lula and Flávio in equal measure, saying that Flávio lost his own convention to an Argentine and an avatar (Folha de S.Paulo, Estadão, Pleno.News). THE FOURTH AXIS is institutional, it is the strongest of the week, and it was born inside the [PL](/en/glossary#pl)'s own convention. On the night of Jul 28, Moraes gave 48 hours for Jair Bolsonaro's defence to say whether he authorised the use of his own image and voice in the artificial-intelligence video shown at Flávio's convention, citing risk of a fresh breach of his precautionary measures (O Globo, G1, Estadão). On Wednesday the defence answered that he did NOT authorise it (Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo, Estadão), while Flávio's campaign told the [TSE](/en/glossary#tse) the video is legal and does not deceive voters (Folha de S.Paulo). The [PT](/en/glossary#pt) petitioned the TSE over another AI video, in which Flávio flies a fighter jet alongside Javier Milei. TSE justices see abuse and want to curb the excessive use of AI in campaigns, and the [STF](/en/glossary#stf) is preparing to act should the TSE not punish (Estadão, O Globo). The same day, Lula publicly complained about corporatism among judges and prosecutors and argued for institutional reform (Folha de S.Paulo), and Dino ordered the government and Congress to specify the responsibility of members of parliament over amendments, with a 10-day deadline (G1, Folha de S.Paulo). Even with all of that piling up, the market on impeachment of an STF justice rose only 0.05pp, to 2.85%, in a book of USD 83,000. Recording the direction is mandatory; building a narrative on it is not, because a 0.05pp move on USD 83,000 is practically stillness. In the Master case, the record is one of method and it is a promotion in status: what the previous day carried as an exclusive report by Valor Econômico, namely that André Mendonça authorised the [Federal Police](/en/glossary#pf) to trace assets abroad belonging to Daniel Vorcaro, appeared on Wednesday in Estadão as well, so it is no longer single-sourced. THE FIFTH AXIS is external. Trump extended the national emergency over Brazil for a year on Jul 28, and on Wednesday the matter changed in nature: the Brazilian government came to read the extension as possible preparation for new sanctions (O Globo, Valor Econômico), and the PL campaign leadership expects US measures against Alexandre de Moraes (O Globo). In parallel, US senators accused the Trump administration of promoting conspiracy theories about the Brazilian elections (G1, CBN). THE SIXTH AXIS is inflation, and it carries a lesson about small books worth more than the number. The modal band went BACK to 5.00% to 5.49%, at 37.95%, while the 4.50% to 4.99% band fell from 39.25% to 34.70% and the 5.50% to 5.99% band collapsed from 12.20% to 3.55%. In other words, the shift the panel recorded yesterday undid itself in a single session. In a book that adds up to USD 80,000 and is NOT covered by the double-reading guard, changing modal band two days in a row is noise, and the honest record is that yesterday's reading did not hold. THE STATE POLLS OF THE DAY do not enter the panel's national window, by scope rule, but their content completes the picture of a split country and now includes the largest electoral college. Genial/[Quaest](/en/glossary#quaest) in São Paulo (n=1,650, field Jul 23 to 27, 2pp margin, BR-09998/2026 and SP-04846/2026) has Flávio 34% x Lula 30% in the first round and Flávio 40% x Lula 35% in the runoff, plus Tarcísio 41% x Haddad 26% in the state race. Genial/Quaest in Bahia has Lula 52% x Flávio 18%, with ACM Neto and Jerônimo Rodrigues in a statistical tie in both rounds. Ipsos-Ipec in Ceará (n=800, field Jul 23 to 26, 3pp margin, BR-07235/2026) has Lula 54% x Flávio 23%. Adding what has already been published, Flávio wins São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, Lula wins the Northeast comfortably and Minas Gerais is a statistical tie. A CAPTURE NOTE, and it is about process. The double-reading guard REJECTED the first round over a 1.00pp divergence in Renan Santos's third place, from 62.50% to 61.50%, and APPROVED the second round with no divergence at all in the five electoral books. There were four readings in total, across sixteen minutes, and the 61.50% published is the value that repeated in the last three. Every price in this update enters firm and there is no range. Yesterday two rounds were blocked and the same kind of thin book showed up again today, which is consistent: first-round third place adds up to USD 484,000 against USD 116.49M in the presidential book, and a wide spread in a book that size is normal. Finally, the calendar: the week still brings PoderData on Jul 30 (n=2,400) and Vox Brasil on Jul 31 (n=2,100) to say whether the 62.50% level has polling behind it, and the Aug 5 deadline for naming running mates still applies to Flávio and to Zema.
